title: Deploy Harmony: week atlas + checklist (May 2027) - WIP
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a working atlas for the May 10-16 deploy week (internal name: Deploy Harmony). Purpose is to consolidate a compact day-by-day calendar, crisp preflight checklist, smoke/rollback criteria, and a short draft of the release notes we’ll ship alongside the console update. Keep this lightweight — intended for on-shift operators and engineers who will be handling cutovers and triage.

Goals:
- Push the console route-level telemetry optimizations and the serving runtime kernel tweak (cpu fallback guard) with minimal user-visible regression.
- Validate latency SLOs in europe-west and us-central under the new batching policy.
- Verify canary-to-wide promotion process (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) completes without surge.

High-level constraints / assumptions:
- Dedicated capacity pools are reserved for the week (commit ID: JIRA-RELEASE-4721).
- Traffic warmup window is 48 hours prior to the 5% ramp.
- Nightly build artifacts are published to s3://redwood-artifacts/nightly/harmony/ (tag: harmony-2027-05-09).
- Primary on-call: eng-release (pager rotated per schedule).

DAY-BY-DAY ATLAS (quick):
- May 08 (Sun): dry-run rehearsal in staging; smoke pass for KV cache invalidation tests.
- May 09 (Mon): artifact freeze 18:00 PT; final QA signoff by QA lead (Priya).
- May 10 (Tue, D0): Canary push to 0.5% in us-central 09:00 PT -> observe 3h telemetry baseline. Smoke checks + SLA gating.
- May 11 (Wed, D1): Expand to 5% across us-central + eu-west if canary stable. Begin warmup.
- May 12 (Thu, D2): Ramp to 25% if all gating green; run synthetic load test targeting 95th p99 latency + error budget check.
- May 13 (Fri, D3): Ramp to 100% (wide) during daytime window 10:00-15:00 PT if telemetry stable. Follow with 4-hour watch party.
- May 14-16 (Sat-Mon): Post-rollout monitoring, incident triage if regressions, and retro capture.

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (must clear before D0):
- [ ] Artifacts: harmony-2027-05-09 pushed and checksum validated. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Release notes draft ready and short customer-facing summary (owner: Elliot).
- [ ] Canary lanes provisioned and routing policies applied (owner: infra team).
- [ ] Dedicated pool health: GPU util < 70% under 30m synthetic (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards prepared (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token counts, cost-per-token) with alert thresholds pre-configured. (owner: observability)
- [ ] Rollback images/states validated and documented (owner: release-eng).
- [ ] Oncall rotas and incident contacts posted to the #release-ops channel (owner: Dana)
- [ ] Customer outbound comms draft (if necessary) pre-approved by comms.

SMOKE & GATING (how we decide to proceed):
- Canary hold conditions (stop and roll back):
  - sustained p99 latency increase > 20% vs baseline for 30m
  - error rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 15m OR > 3x relative increase
  - token-cost per request increased > 15% without throughput benefit
- Promotion gating to next phase requires: canary stable for 3h AND no open Sev2/Sev1 tickets against the deploy artifacts.
- If an alert fires, the deployment lead (Priya) calls the rollcall within 10 minutes; immediate rollback if gating threshold breached and repeated in 3 consecutive samples.

ROLLBACK PROCEDURE (quick):
1) Pause traffic ramp in routing console.
2) Flip routing to prior model variant (pin via API) and drain new instances.
3) Revert config in infra repo (PR template included) and trigger hotfix build.
4) Notify SRE & CS; open rollback incident with notes in Confluence.

POST-DEPLOY WATCHLIST (first 24h):
- watch: p99 latency, error budget burn, new metric: prefix-cache-hit-rate, kv-cache memory pressure.
- run: 30-minute synthetic suite every 2h for first 8 hours.
- phone-home: any user-facing 500/502 spikes -> page eng-release immediately.

CHANGELOG / RELEASE NOTES (draft — short):
Title: "Console telemetry aggregation & serving runtime batch tuning (May 2027)"
Short summary: Improved route-level telemetry aggregation and a backend kernel change that reduces tail latency for medium-length sequences. Ideal for customer workloads with frequent short-turn prompts.
Highlights:
- server: optimized continuous batching heuristics that reduce p99 latency for 2-8 token prompts by ~12% in internal tests.
- console: route telemetry now reports token-level cost and inferred model variant routing for easier cost attribution.
- infra: guard added to fall back to cpu-safe kernels when quantized kernels observe memory pressure.
Known issues / caveats:
- We expect minor telemetry lag (up to 90s) for the first hour while new aggregation windows warm up.
- A subset (<0.1%) of very long-running KV-cache sessions may experience a transient reconnect; automatic retries are in place.
Customer impact: None expected for majority of users; latency-sensitive workloads will benefit. Standard rate-limiting and quotas unchanged.

SUPPORT RUNBOOK (for CS & Ops):
- If customer reports latency regression: collect route id, example prompt, timestamp, SKU, region, and send to #release-ops. Attach full request id and model variant.
- If there are billing/cost concerns: use the new per-token dashboard to trace high-cost customers and apply temporary quota limits if needed.

NOTES TO SELF / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Q: Should we enable the prefix cache TTL reduction for Dedicated pools in this deploy, or postpone? (Marco: prefer toggle-off for Dedicated; decision pending)
- Q: Do we want an explicit customer-facing blurb for the console that highlights cost breakdown? (Dana to coordinate with comms)
- TODO: add checklist item to confirm canary region infra network egress policies (security sign-off).
- TODO: record quick video snippet showing the telemetry dashboard changes for internal training.

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS & REFERENCES:
- Staging runbook: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-187
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/928, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/451
- Tickets: JIRA-RELEASE-4721, JIRA-OBS-1902
- Slack: #release-ops (pinned messages include the watchlist and escalation ladder)

RETRO FRAME (post-deploy): capture at /confluence/releases/harmony-2027/retro — fill sections: what went well, what failed, near misses, telemetry gaps, action items (owner/time).

END.

(Working doc — expect edits. If you take ownership of any checklist item, add your name next to it and update the status.)
